_comment: Golden tasks for core/skills/consolidate/SKILL.md. Six numbered steps plus step 0 — the routing
sentence under `## When to use it`, numbered 0 so the pass accounting stays a clean 1..6.
TWO cases are bound: step 0 (load-bearing, the schema-budget containment) and step 1 (census, the
retire-when walk doctor already reports). The other five are adjudicated unbindable.
This _comment read `Six steps, three bound` until Copilot round 1 on #360. It was written when
step 5 was classed bound, and it did not move when the pre-commit checkpoint reclassified that row
to `already-carried` — a file's own summary disagreeing with its own cases, which is proposal 0020
one line up from the thing it describes.

mandate.quote: Every record carries a `Retire when:` line

_note: A CENSUS ROW: `doctor` already walks these records and prints `every record states a retirement
condition`. It REPORTS rather than fails — cli/doctor.mjs says so in as many words, `no rule
mandates the field, and doctor does not enforce what nobody legislated`. This row records that
the skill DOES mandate it, and re-indexes the existing figure under the mandate that wants it.
The carrier is proven by IMPORT: this corpus's runner imports RETIRE_WHEN from doctor.mjs, so a
carrier that stops exporting it fails at load. That proves doctor CONTAINS the check, never that
it RUNS it — the second half is drills' subject and is named, not claimed.

cases.why: Whether a record holds exactly one fact — asked in both directions, merge and split — is the granularity judgement this step exists to exercise. The record_kilobytes budget bounds SIZE, which is a proxy nobody should mistake for the question.

Surfacing a contradiction rather than overwriting it is a judgement about meaning across two records. No artifact records the contradictions that were correctly surfaced, and a store with none looks identical to one nobody read.

Compression and demotion leave a smaller record and a changed narrative, and neither carries a mark saying a consolidation pass produced it. The git history holds the act; the tree holds only the outcome.

The index being generated and byte-compared is held by .portulan/verify/index.sh on every run, and that rail is itself drilled. A case here would be a third carrier of a rule two already hold. This row shipped as `bound` with carrier `index` until the pre-commit checkpoint moved index.sh out of the tree and watched the corpus stay green: the runner never reads the carrier field, so the row bound nothing and inflated the headline by one.

Filing a consolidation as a change for review rather than as a fact is the human gate, and what checks it is the platform floor plus docs.sh's proposal rules in bash. Binding it here would be the same language-boundary duplication codify step 4 is unbindable for.

_note: STEP 0 IS NOT A PASS STEP — it is the `When to use it` routing sentence, which decides which move
applies and names every budget by id. It is numbered 0 so the pass-step accounting above stays a
clean 1..6 and this row cannot be mistaken for one of them.
Both sides are derived: the ids come from spec/workspace.schema.json's memory budget properties,
and containment is tested against the skill's own text. A fifth budget, or a rename, reddens this
— which is the staleness nothing in the tree could see before.
